_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Into the wilderness the Spirit leads us, hungry and tried.
We do not live by bread alone.
Every word from the mouth of God is our bread.
We will worship the Lord and serve only him.
When we were caught and ashamed, God did not leave us.
You are our hiding place; you surround us with deliverance.
Come, let us worship the One who meets us in the wild.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Forty days the wilderness stretches before us: dry wind, bare stone, an empty stomach, a tempter's easy voice.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
You know this country. Adam knew it, reaching for the fruit; you walked it yourself, hungry and unbroken.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
So when the voice says turn these stones to bread, says bow down, says throw yourself down, teach us your one answer.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
For you are our hiding place; when we confess, the guilt we carried lifts like fog burning off.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
Come into the wilderness unafraid; the angels are already on their way. Come, let us worship.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross. Lead us through. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The Spirit drives us out where the bread runs out.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
We do not live by bread alone, but by God's every word.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
You are our hiding place; you surround us with deliverance.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross.
Come, let us worship the One who meets us in the wild.
We are pilgrims on the way to the cross. Amen.
